content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
content.english: This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph

content.latin: Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
content.english: Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness

content.latin: Hac die lætus méruit suprémos
content.english: On this feast day year by year receiveth

content.latin: Laudis honóres.
content.english: Merited honors.

content.latin: Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
content.english: Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,

content.latin: Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
content.english: Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.

content.latin: Donec humános animávit auræ
content.english: While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,

content.latin: Spíritus artus.
content.english: Quickened his being.

content.latin: Cuius ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
content.english: Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,

content.latin: Ægra quæ passim iacuére membra,
content.english: Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,

content.latin: Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
content.english: Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,

content.latin: Restituúntur.
content.english: At his petition.

content.latin: Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
content.english: Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,

content.latin: Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
content.english: Chanting his praises with devout affection,

content.latin: Ut piis eius précibus iuvémur
content.english: That in his merits we may have a portion,

content.latin: Omne per ævum.
content.english: Now and forever.

content.latin: Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
content.english: His be the glory, power and salvation,

content.latin: Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
content.english: Who over all things reigneth in the highest,

content.latin: Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
content.english: Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,

content.latin: Trinus et unus.
content.english: Onely and Trinal.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: At the Nocturn

content.latin: Ant. In Deo salutáre meum * et glória mea: et spes mea in Deo est.
content.english: Ant. In God is my salvation * and my glory: and my hope is in God.

content.latin: Psalmus 61 [1]
content.english: Psalm 61 [1]

content.latin: 61:2 Nonne Deo subiécta erit ánima mea? * ab ipso enim salutáre meum.
content.english: 61:2 Shall not my soul be subject to God? * for from him is my salvation.

content.latin: 61:3 Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus: * suscéptor meus, non movébor ámplius.
content.english: 61:3 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.

content.latin: 61:4 Quoúsque irrúitis in hóminem? * interfícitis univérsi vos: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ?
content.english: 61:4 How long do you rush in upon a man? * you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.

content.latin: 61:5 Verúmtamen prétium meum cogitavérunt repéllere, cucúrri in siti: * ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant.
content.english: 61:5 But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: * they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.

content.latin: 61:6 Verúmtamen Deo subiécta esto, ánima mea: * quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea.
content.english: 61:6 But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: * for from him is my patience.

content.latin: 61:7 Quia ipse Deus meus, et salvátor meus: * adiútor meus, non emigrábo.
content.english: 61:7 For he is my God and my saviour: * he is my helper, I shall not be moved.

content.latin: 61:8 In Deo salutáre meum, et glória mea: * Deus auxílii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
content.english: 61:8 In God is my salvation and my glory: * he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.

content.latin: 61:9 Speráte in eo omnis congregátio pópuli, effúndite coram illo corda vestra: * Deus adiútor noster in ætérnum.
content.english: 61:9 Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. * God is our helper for ever.

content.latin: 61:10 Verúmtamen vani fílii hóminum, mendáces fílii hóminum in statéris: * ut decípiant ipsi de vanitáte in idípsum.
content.english: 61:10 But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: * that by vanity they may together deceive.

content.latin: 61:11 Nolíte speráre in iniquitáte, et rapínas nolíte concupíscere: * divítiæ si áffluant, nolíte cor appónere.
content.english: 61:11 Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: * if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.

content.latin: 61:12 Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi, quia potéstas Dei est, et tibi, Dómine, misericórdia: * quia tu reddes unicuíque iuxta ópera sua.
content.english: 61:12 God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God, and mercy to thee, O Lord; * for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.

content.english: Ant. Behold the works of the Lord * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

content.latin: 65:1 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * date glóriam laudi eius.
content.english: 65:1 Shout with joy to God, all the earth, sing ye a psalm to his name; * give glory to his praise.

content.latin: 65:3 Dícite Deo: Quam terribília sunt ópera tua, Dómine! * in multitúdine virtútis tuæ mentiéntur tibi inimíci tui.
content.english: 65:3 Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! * in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.

content.latin: 65:4 Omnis terra adóret te, et psallat tibi: * psalmum dicat nómini tuo.
content.english: 65:4 Let all the earth adore thee, * and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.

content.latin: 65:5 Veníte, et vidéte ópera Dei: * terríbilis in consíliis super fílios hóminum.
content.english: 65:5 Come and see the works of God; * who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.

content.latin: 65:6 Qui convértit mare in áridam, in flúmine pertransíbunt pede: * ibi lætábimur in ipso.
content.english: 65:6 Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: * there shall we rejoice in him.

content.latin: 65:7 Qui dominátur in virtúte sua in ætérnum, óculi eius super gentes respíciunt: * qui exásperant non exalténtur in semetípsis.
content.english: 65:7 Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; * let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.

content.latin: 65:8 Benedícite, gentes, Deum nostrum: * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius,
content.english: 65:8 O bless our God, ye Gentiles: * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

content.latin: 65:9 Qui pósuit ánimam meam ad vitam: * et non dedit in commotiónem pedes meos.
content.english: 65:9 Who hath set my soul to live: * and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:

content.latin: 65:10 Quóniam probásti nos, Deus: * igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum.
content.english: 65:10 For thou, O God, hast proved us: * thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.

content.latin: 65:11 Induxísti nos in láqueum, posuísti tribulatiónes in dorso nostro: * imposuísti hómines super cápita nostra.
content.english: 65:11 Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back: * thou hast set men over our heads.

content.latin: 65:12 Transívimus per ignem et aquam: * et eduxísti nos in refrigérium.
content.english: 65:12 We have passed through fire and water, * and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Ant. Vidéte ópera Dómini, et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius.
content.english: Ant. Behold the works of the Lord and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

content.latin: Ant. Audíte, omnes * qui timétis Deum, quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
content.english: Ant. Come and hear, all ye that fear God * what great things he hath done for my soul.

content.latin: 65:13 Introíbo in domum tuam in holocáustis: * reddam tibi vota mea, quæ distinxérunt lábia mea.
content.english: 65:13 I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: * I will pay thee my vows, which my lips have uttered,

content.latin: 65:14 Et locútum est os meum, * in tribulatióne mea.
content.english: 65:14 And my mouth hath spoken, * when I was in trouble.

content.latin: 65:15 Holocáusta medulláta ófferam tibi cum incénso aríetum: * ófferam tibi boves cum hircis.
content.english: 65:15 I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: * I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.

content.latin: 65:16 Veníte, audíte, et narrábo, omnes, qui timétis Deum: * quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 65:16 Come and hear, all ye that fear God, * and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.

content.latin: 65:17 Ad ipsum ore meo clamávi, * et exaltávi sub lingua mea.
content.english: 65:17 I cried to him with my mouth: * and I extolled him with my tongue.

content.latin: 65:18 Iniquitátem si aspéxi in corde meo, * non exáudiet Dóminus.
content.english: 65:18 If I have looked at iniquity in my heart, * the Lord will not hear me.

content.latin: 65:19 Proptérea exaudívit Deus, * et atténdit voci deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 65:19 Therefore hath God heard me, * and hath attended to the voice of my supplication.

content.latin: 65:20 Benedíctus Deus, * qui non amóvit oratiónem meam, et misericórdiam suam a me.
content.english: 65:20 Blessed be God, * who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.

content.english: Ant. Let God arise, * and let his enemies be scattered. ‡

content.latin: 67:2 Exsúrgat Deus, et dissipéntur inimíci eius, * ‡ et fúgiant qui odérunt eum, a fácie eius.
content.english: 67:2 Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: * ‡ and let them that hate him flee from before his face.

content.latin: 67:3 Sicut déficit fumus, defíciant: * sicut fluit cera a fácie ignis, sic péreant peccatóres a fácie Dei.
content.english: 67:3 As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: * as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

content.latin: 67:4 Et iusti epuléntur, et exsúltent in conspéctu Dei: * et delecténtur in lætítia.
content.english: 67:4 And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: * and be delighted with gladness.

content.latin: 67:5 Cantáte Deo, psalmum dícite nómini eius: * iter fácite ei, qui ascéndit super occásum: (fit reverentia) Dóminus nomen illi.
content.english: 67:5 Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, * make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: (bow head) the Lord is his name.

content.latin: 67:5 Exsultáte in conspéctu eius: * turbabúntur a fácie eius, patris orphanórum et iúdicis viduárum.
content.english: 67:5 Rejoice ye before him: * but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence, who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows.

content.latin: 67:6 Deus in loco sancto suo: * Deus, qui inhabitáre facit uníus moris in domo:
content.english: 67:6 God in his holy place: * God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house:

content.latin: 67:7 Qui edúcit vinctos in fortitúdine, * simíliter eos qui exásperant, qui hábitant in sepúlcris.
content.english: 67:7 Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; * in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.

content.latin: 67:8 Deus, cum egrederéris in conspéctu pópuli tui, * cum pertransíres in desérto:
content.english: 67:8 O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, * when thou didst pass through the desert:

content.latin: 67:9 Terra mota est, étenim cæli distillavérunt a fácie Dei Sínai, * a fácie Dei Israël.
content.english: 67:9 The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sinai, * at the presence of the God of Israel.

content.latin: 67:10 Plúviam voluntáriam segregábis, Deus, hereditáti tuæ: * et infirmáta est, tu vero perfecísti eam.
content.english: 67:10 Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, * O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.

content.latin: 67:11 Animália tua habitábunt in ea: * parásti in dulcédine tua páuperi, Deus.
content.english: 67:11 In it shall thy animals dwell; * in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered.

content.latin: Ant. Deus noster, * Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
content.english: Ant. Our God * is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.

content.latin: 67:12 Dóminus dabit verbum evangelizántibus, * virtúte multa.
content.english: 67:12 The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings, * with great power.

content.latin: 67:13 Rex virtútum dilécti, dilécti: * et speciéi domus divídere spólia.
content.english: 67:13 The king of powers is of the beloved, * of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.

content.latin: 67:14 Si dormiátis inter médios cleros, pennæ colúmbæ deargentátæ, * et posterióra dorsi eius in pallóre auri.
content.english: 67:14 If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, * and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.

content.latin: 67:15 Dum discérnit cæléstis reges super eam, nive dealbabúntur in Selmon: * mons Dei, mons pinguis.
content.english: 67:15 When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon. * The mountain of God is a fat mountain,

content.latin: 67:16 Mons coagulátus, mons pinguis: * ut quid suspicámini montes coagulátos?
content.english: 67:16 a curdled mountain, a fat mountain; * Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?

content.latin: 67:17 Mons, in quo beneplácitum est Deo habitáre in eo: * étenim Dóminus habitábit in finem.
content.english: 67:17 A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: * for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.

content.latin: 67:18 Currus Dei decem míllibus múltiplex, míllia lætántium: * Dóminus in eis in Sina in sancto.
content.english: 67:18 The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: * the Lord is among them in Sinai, in the holy place.

content.latin: 67:19 Ascendísti in altum, cepísti captivitátem: * accepísti dona in homínibus.
content.english: 67:19 Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; * thou hast received gifts in men.

content.latin: 67:19 Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum.
content.english: 67:19 Yea for those also that do not believe, * the dwelling of the Lord God.

content.latin: 67:20 Benedíctus Dóminus die cotídie: * prósperum iter fáciet nobis Deus salutárium nostrórum.
content.english: 67:20 Blessed be the Lord day by day: * the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.

content.latin: 67:21 Deus noster, Deus salvos faciéndi: * et Dómini Dómini éxitus mortis.
content.english: 67:21 Our God is the God of salvation: * and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.

content.latin: 67:22 Verúmtamen Deus confrínget cápita inimicórum suórum: * vérticem capílli perambulántium in delíctis suis.
content.english: 67:22 But God shall break the heads of his enemies: * the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.

content.latin: 67:23 Dixit Dóminus: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris:
content.english: 67:23 The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, * I will turn them into the depth of the sea:

content.latin: 67:24 Ut intingátur pes tuus in sánguine: * lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso.
content.english: 67:24 That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; * the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: Ant. Our God is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.

content.latin: Ant. In ecclésiis * benedícite Dómino Deo.
content.english: Ant. In the churches * bless ye God the Lord.

content.latin: 67:25 Vidérunt ingréssus tuos, Deus: * ingréssus Dei mei: regis mei qui est in sancto.
content.english: 67:25 They have seen thy goings, O God, * the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.

content.latin: 67:26 Prævenérunt príncipes coniúncti psalléntibus: * in médio iuvenculárum tympanistriárum.
content.english: 67:26 Princes went before joined with singers, * in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.

content.latin: 67:27 In ecclésiis benedícite Deo Dómino, * de fóntibus Israël.
content.english: 67:27 In the churches bless ye God the Lord, * from the fountains of Israel.

content.latin: 67:28 Ibi Béniamin adolescéntulus: * in mentis excéssu.
content.english: 67:28 There is Benjamin a youth, * in ecstasy of mind.

content.latin: 67:28 Príncipes Iuda, duces eórum: * príncipes Zábulon, príncipes Néphtali.
content.english: 67:28 The princes of Juda are their leaders: * the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.

content.latin: 67:29 Manda, Deus, virtúti tuæ: * confírma hoc, Deus, quod operátus es in nobis.
content.english: 67:29 Command thy strength, O God: * confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.

content.latin: 67:30 A templo tuo in Ierúsalem, * tibi ófferent reges múnera.
content.english: 67:30 From thy temple in Jerusalem, * kings shall offer presents to thee.

content.latin: 67:31 Íncrepa feras arúndinis, congregátio taurórum in vaccis populórum: * ut exclúdant eos, qui probáti sunt argénto.
content.english: 67:31 Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; * who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver.

content.latin: 67:31 Díssipa gentes, quæ bella volunt: vénient legáti ex Ægýpto: * Æthiópia prævéniet manus eius Deo.
content.english: 67:31 Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: * Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.

content.latin: 67:33 Regna terræ, cantáte Deo: * psállite Dómino.
content.english: 67:33 Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: * sing ye to the Lord:

content.latin: 67:33 Psállite Deo, qui ascéndit super cælum cæli, * ad Oriéntem.
content.english: 67:33 Sing ye to God, who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, * to the east.

content.latin: 67:34 Ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis, date glóriam Deo super Israël, * magnificéntia eius, et virtus eius in núbibus.
content.english: 67:34 Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power: give ye glory to God for Israel, * his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.

content.latin: 67:36 Mirábilis Deus in sanctis suis, Deus Israël ipse dabit virtútem, et fortitúdinem plebi suæ, * benedíctus Deus.
content.english: 67:36 God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people; * blessed be God.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. In the churches bless ye God the Lord.

content.latin: Ant. Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam. ‡
content.english: Ant. Save me, O God * for the waters are come in even unto my soul. ‡

content.latin: 68:2 Salvum me fac, Deus: quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
content.english: 68:2 Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

content.latin: 68:3 ‡ Infíxus sum in limo profúndi: * et non est substántia.
content.english: 68:3 ‡ I stick fast in the mire of the deep: * and there is no sure standing.

content.latin: 68:3 Veni in altitúdinem maris: * et tempéstas demérsit me.
content.english: 68:3 I am come into the depth of the sea: * and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.

content.latin: 68:4 Laborávi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ: * defecérunt óculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.
content.english: 68:4 I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse: * my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.

content.latin: 68:5 Multiplicáti sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, * qui odérunt me gratis.
content.english: 68:5 They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, * who hate me without cause.

content.latin: 68:5 Confortáti sunt qui persecúti sunt me inimíci mei iniúste: * quæ non rápui, tunc exsolvébam.
content.english: 68:5 My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: * then did I pay that which I took not away.

content.latin: 68:6 Deus, tu scis insipiéntiam meam: * et delícta mea a te non sunt abscóndita.
content.english: 68:6 O God, thou knowest my foolishness; * and my offences are not hidden from thee.

content.latin: 68:7 Non erubéscant in me qui exspéctant te, Dómine, * Dómine virtútum.
content.english: 68:7 Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, * the Lord of hosts.

content.latin: 68:7 Non confundántur super me * qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.
content.english: 68:7 Let them not be confounded on my account, * who seek thee, O God of Israel.

content.latin: 68:8 Quóniam propter te sustínui oppróbrium: * opéruit confúsio fáciem meam.
content.english: 68:8 Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; * shame hath covered my face.

content.latin: 68:9 Extráneus factus sum frátribus meis, * et peregrínus fíliis matris meæ.
content.english: 68:9 I am become a stranger to my brethren, * and an alien to the sons of my mother.

content.latin: 68:10 Quóniam zelus domus tuæ comédit me: * et oppróbria exprobrántium tibi cecidérunt super me.
content.english: 68:10 For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: * and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.

content.latin: 68:11 Et opérui in ieiúnio ánimam meam: * et factum est in oppróbrium mihi.
content.english: 68:11 And I covered my soul in fasting: * and it was made a reproach to me.

content.latin: 68:12 Et pósui vestiméntum meum cilícium: * et factus sum illis in parábolam.
content.english: 68:12 And I made haircloth my garment: * and I became a byword to them.

content.latin: 68:13 Advérsum me loquebántur, qui sedébant in porta: * et in me psallébant qui bibébant vinum.
content.english: 68:13 They that sat in the gate spoke against me: * and they that drank wine made me their song.

content.latin: 68:13 Ego vero oratiónem meam ad te, Dómine: * tempus benepláciti, Deus.
content.english: 68:13 But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; * for the time of thy good pleasure, O God.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salvum me fac, Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam.
content.english: Ant. Save me, O God for the waters are come in even unto my soul.

content.latin: Ant. Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, save me * from my enemies.

content.latin: 68:14 In multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ exáudi me, * in veritáte salútis tuæ:
content.english: 68:14 In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, * in the truth of thy salvation.

content.latin: 68:15 Éripe me de luto, ut non infígar: * líbera me ab iis, qui odérunt me, et de profúndis aquárum.
content.english: 68:15 Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: * deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.

content.latin: 68:16 Non me demérgat tempéstas aquæ, neque absórbeat me profúndum: * neque úrgeat super me púteus os suum.
content.english: 68:16 Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: * and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.

content.latin: 68:17 Exáudi me, Dómine, quóniam benígna est misericórdia tua: * secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum réspice in me.
content.english: 68:17 Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; * look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.

content.latin: 68:18 Et ne avértas fáciem tuam a púero tuo: * quóniam tríbulor, velóciter exáudi me.
content.english: 68:18 And turn not away thy face from thy servant: * for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.

content.latin: 68:19 Inténde ánimæ meæ, et líbera eam: * propter inimícos meos éripe me.
content.english: 68:19 Attend to my soul, and deliver it: * save me because of my enemies.

content.latin: 68:20 Tu scis impropérium meum, et confusiónem meam, * et reveréntiam meam.
content.english: 68:20 Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, * and my shame.

content.latin: 68:21 In conspéctu tuo sunt omnes qui tríbulant me: * impropérium exspectávit cor meum, et misériam.
content.english: 68:21 In thy sight are all they that afflict me; * my heart hath expected reproach and misery.

content.latin: 68:21 Et sustínui qui simul contristarétur, et non fuit: * et qui consolarétur, et non invéni.
content.english: 68:21 And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, * but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.

content.latin: 68:22 Et dedérunt in escam meam fel: * et in siti mea potavérunt me acéto.
content.english: 68:22 And they gave me gall for my food, * and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

content.latin: 68:23 Fiat mensa eórum coram ipsis in láqueum, * et in retributiónes, et in scándalum.
content.english: 68:23 Let their table become as a snare before them, * and a recompense, and a stumblingblock.

content.latin: 68:24 Obscuréntur óculi eórum ne vídeant: * et dorsum eórum semper incúrva.
content.english: 68:24 Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; * and their back bend thou down always.

content.latin: 68:25 Effúnde super eos iram tuam: * et furor iræ tuæ comprehéndat eos.
content.english: 68:25 Pour out thy indignation upon them: * and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.

content.latin: 68:26 Fiat habitátio eórum desérta: * et in tabernáculis eórum non sit qui inhábitet.
content.english: 68:26 Let their habitation be made desolate: * and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.

content.latin: 68:27 Quóniam quem tu percussísti, persecúti sunt: * et super dolórem vúlnerum meórum addidérunt.
content.english: 68:27 Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; * and they have added to the grief of my wounds.

content.latin: 68:28 Appóne iniquitátem super iniquitátem eórum: * et non intrent in iustítiam tuam.
content.english: 68:28 Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: * and let them not come into thy justice.

content.latin: 68:29 Deleántur de libro vivéntium: * et cum iustis non scribántur.
content.english: 68:29 Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; * and with the just let them not be written.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Propter inimícos meos éripe me, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. O Lord, save me from my enemies.

content.latin: Ant. Quǽrite Dóminum, * et vivet ánima vestra.
content.english: Ant. Look for the Lord * and your soul shall live.

content.latin: 68:30 Ego sum pauper et dolens: * salus tua, Deus, suscépit me.
content.english: 68:30 I am poor and sorrowful: * thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.

content.latin: 68:31 Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico: * et magnificábo eum in laude:
content.english: 68:31 I will praise the name of God with a canticle: * and I will magnify him with praise.

content.latin: 68:32 Et placébit Deo super vítulum novéllum: * córnua producéntem et úngulas.
content.english: 68:32 And it shall please God better than a young calf, * that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.

content.latin: 68:33 Vídeant páuperes et læténtur: * quǽrite Deum, et vivet ánima vestra.
content.english: 68:33 Let the poor see and rejoice: * seek ye God, and your soul shall live.

content.latin: 68:34 Quóniam exaudívit páuperes Dóminus: * et vinctos suos non despéxit.
content.english: 68:34 For the Lord hath heard the poor: * and hath not despised his prisoners.

content.latin: 68:35 Laudent illum cæli et terra, * mare et ómnia reptília in eis.
content.english: 68:35 Let the heavens and the earth praise him; * the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.

content.latin: 68:36 Quóniam Deus salvam fáciet Sion: * et ædificabúntur civitátes Iuda.
content.english: 68:36 For God will save Sion, * and the cities of Juda shall be built up.

content.latin: 68:36 Et inhabitábunt ibi, * et hereditáte acquírent eam.
content.english: 68:36 And they shall dwell there, * and acquire it by inheritance.

content.latin: 68:37 Et semen servórum eius possidébit eam: * et qui díligunt nomen eius, habitábunt in ea.
content.english: 68:37 And the seed of his servants shall possess it; * and they that love his name shall dwell therein.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Quǽrite Dóminum, et vivet ánima vestra.
content.english: Ant. Look for the Lord and your soul shall live.

content.latin: ℣. Laudábo nomen Dei cum cántico.
content.english: ℣. I will praise the name of God.

content.latin: ℟. Et magnificábo eum in laude.
content.english: ℟. And I will magnify him with praise.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De libro primo Regum
content.english: Lesson from the first book of Samuel

content.latin: 6 Dixit autem Iónathas ad adolescéntem armígerum suum: Veni, transeámus ad statiónem incircumcisórum horum, si forte fáciat Dóminus pro nobis, quia non est Dómino diffícile salváre vel in multis vel in paucis.
content.english: 6 And Jonathan said to the young man that bore his armour: Come, let us go over to the garrison of these uncircumcised, it may be the Lord will do for us, because it is easy for the Lord to save either by many, or by few.

content.latin: 7 Dixítque ei ármiger suus: Fac ómnia, quæ placent ánimo tuo, perge quo cupis, et ero tecum ubicúmque volúeris.
content.english: 7 And his armourbearer said to him: Do all that pleaseth thy mind: go whither thou wilt, and I will be with thee wheresoever thou hast a mind.

content.latin: 8 Et ait Iónathas: Ecce nos transímus ad viros istos. Cumque apparuérimus eis,
content.english: 8 And Jonathan said: Behold we will go over to these men. And when we shall be seen by them,

content.latin: 9 Si táliter locúti fúerint ad nos: Manéte donec veniámus ad vos; stemus in loco nostro nec ascendámus ad eos.
content.english: 9 If they shall speak thus to us: Stay till we come to you: let us stand still in our place, and not go up to them.

content.latin: 10 Si autem díxerint: Ascéndite ad nos; ascendámus, quia trádidit eos Dóminus in mánibus nostris: hoc erit nobis signum.
content.english: 10 But if they shall say: Come up to us: let us go up, because the Lord hath delivered them into our hands, this shall be a sign unto us.

content.latin: 11 Appáruit ígitur utérque statióni Philísthiim. Dixerúntque Philísthiim: En Hebrǽi egrediúntur de cavérnis, in quibus abscónditi fúerant.
content.english: 11 So both of them discovered themselves to the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said: Behold the Hebrews come forth out of the holes wherein they were hid.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Euge, serve bone et fidélis, quia in pauca fuísti fidélis, supra multa te constítuam:
content.english: ℟. Well done, thou good and faithful servant, thou hast been faithful over a few things. I will make thee ruler over many things:

content.latin: * Intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
content.english: * Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, quinque talénta tradidísti mihi, ecce ália quinque superlucrátus sum.
content.english: ℣. Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents; behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

content.latin: ℟. Intra in gáudium Dómini tui.
content.english: ℟. Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. He whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocate with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 12 Et locúti sunt viri de statióne ad Iónatham et ad armígerum eius, dixerúntque: Ascéndite ad nos, et ostendámus vobis rem. Et ait Iónathas ad armígerum suum: Ascendámus, séquere me; trádidit enim Dóminus eos in manus Israël.
content.english: 12 And the men of the garrison spoke to Jonathan, and to his armourbearer, and said: Come up to us, and we will show you a thing. And Jonathan said to his armourbearer: Let us go up, follow me: for the Lord hath delivered them into the hands of Israel.

content.latin: 13 Ascéndit autem Iónathas mánibus et pédibus reptans et ármiger eius post eum. Itaque álii cadébant ante Iónatham, álios ármiger eius interficiébat sequens eum.
content.english: 13 And Jonathan went up creeping on his hands and feet, and his armourbearer after him. And some fell before Jonathan, others his armourbearer slew as he followed him.

content.latin: 14 Et facta est plaga prima, qua percússit Iónathas et ármiger eius, quasi vigínti virórum, in média parte iúgeri, quam par boum in die aráre consuévit.
content.english: 14 And the first slaughter which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was of about twenty men, within half an acre of land, which a yoke of oxen is wont to plough in a day.

content.latin: 15 Et factum est miráculum in castris per agros; sed et omnis pópulus statiónis eórum, qui íerant ad prædándum, obstúpuit, et conturbáta est terra, et áccidit quasi miráculum a Deo.
content.english: 15 And there was a miracle in the camp, through the fields: yea and all the people of their garrison, who had gone out to plunder, were amazed, and the earth trembled: and it happened as a miracle from God.

content.latin: 16 Et respexérunt speculatóres Saul, qui erant in Gábaa Béniamin, et ecce multitúdo prostráta et huc illúcque diffúgiens.
content.english: 16 And the watchmen of Saul, who were in Gabaa of Benjamin looked, and behold a multitude overthrown, and fleeing this way and that.

content.latin: 17 Et ait Saul pópulo, qui erat cum eo: Requírite et vidéte quis abíerit ex nobis. Cumque requisíssent, repértum est non adésse Iónatham et armígerum eius.
content.english: 17 And Saul said to the people that were with him: Look, and see who is gone from us. And when they had sought, it was found that Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.

content.latin: 18 Et ait Saul ad Achíam: Applica arcam Dei (erat enim ibi arca Dei in die illa cum fíliis Israël).
content.english: 18 And Saul said to Achias: Bring the ark of the Lord. (For the ark of God was there that day with the children of Israel.)

content.latin: 19 Cumque loquerétur Saul ad sacerdótem, tumúltus magnus exórtus est in castris Philisthinórum, crescebátque paulátim et clárius resonábat. Et ait Saul ad sacerdótem: Cóntrahe manum tuam.
content.english: 19 And while Saul spoke to the priest, there arose a great uproar in the camp of the Philistines: and it increased by degrees, and was heard more clearly. And Saul said to the priest: Draw in thy hand.

content.latin: 20 Conclamávit ergo Saul, et omnis pópulus, qui erat cum eo, et venérunt usque ad locum certáminis; et ecce versus fúerat gládius uniuscuiúsque ad próximum suum, et cædes magna nimis.
content.english: 20 Then Saul and all the people that were with him, shouted together, and they came to the place of the fight: and behold every man's sword was turned upon his neighbour, and there was a very great slaughter.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Iste cognóvit iustítiam, et vidit mirabília magna, et exorávit Altíssimum:
content.english: ℟. This is he which knew righteousness, and saw great wonders, and made his prayer unto the Most High;

content.latin: * Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
content.english: * And he is numbered among the Saints.

content.latin: ℣. Iste est qui contémpsit vitam mundi, et pervénit ad cæléstia regna.
content.english: ℣. This is he which loved not his life in this world, and is come unto an everlasting kingdom.

content.latin: ℟. Et invéntus est in número Sanctórum.
content.english: ℟. And he is numbered among the Saints.

content.latin: Ephræm, génere Syrus, Nisibéno patre natus est. Adhuc iúvenis ad sanctum Iacóbum epíscopum se cóntulit, a quo baptizátus, brevi ita sanctitáte et doctrína profécit, ut in schola Nísibi, Mesopotámiæ urbe, florénte magíster fúerit constitútus. Edessénæ ecclésiæ diáconus ordinátus et ob humilitátem sacerdótium recúsans, ómnium virtútum splendóre enítuit, et pietátem et religiónem vera sapiéntiæ professióne sibi comparáre satégit. Univérsa illíus ópera, tam spléndido doctrínæ lúmine reférta, effecérunt, ut idem Sanctus, adhuc vivens, tamquam Ecclésiæ Doctor, magno honóre hábitus fúerit. In mirífica ac pia devotióne erga Vírginem Immaculátam primum excélluit. Méritis plenus, Edéssæ in Mesopotámia, décimo quarto kaléndas iúlii, decéssit sub Valénte príncipe: eúmque Benedíctus Papa décimus quintus, ex Sacrórum Rítuum Congregatiónis consúlto, universális Ecclésiæ Doctórem declarávit.
content.english: Ephraem was of Syrian stock, his father being a citizen of Nisibis. While he was still young, he went to the holy bishop James to be baptized. In a short time he advanced so much in holiness and learning that he was made master of a flourishing school at Nisibis, a city in Mesopotamia. Ordained deacon of the Church of Edessa, and refusing the priesthood out of humility, he shone with the splendour of all virtues, and sought to acquire devotion and religion by the profession of true wisdom. All his works, illuminated with the bright light of learning, caused this Saint to be treated with great honour as a Doctor of the Church even in his lifetime. He excelled, above all, in a wonderful and loving devotion to the Immaculate Virgin. Rich in merits, he died on the 18th day of June at Edessa in Mesopotamia, under the Emperor Valens. Pope Benedict XV, after consulting the Congregation of Sacred Rites, declared him a Doctor of the Universal Church.

content.latin: 97:1 Cantáte Dómino cánticum novum: * quia mirabília fecit.

content.latin: 97:1 Salvávit sibi déxtera eius: * et brácchium sanctum eius.

content.latin: 97:2 Notum fecit Dóminus salutáre suum: * in conspéctu géntium revelávit iustítiam suam.
content.english: 97:2 The Lord hath made known his salvation: * he hath revealed his justice in the sight of the Gentiles.

content.latin: 97:3 Recordátus est misericórdiæ suæ, * et veritátis suæ dómui Israël.
content.english: 97:3 He hath remembered his mercy * and his truth toward the house of Israel.

content.latin: 97:3 Vidérunt omnes términi terræ * salutáre Dei nostri.

content.latin: 97:4 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * cantáte, et exsultáte, et psállite.
content.english: 97:4 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; * make melody, rejoice and sing.

content.latin: 97:5 Psállite Dómino in cíthara, in cíthara et voce psalmi: * in tubis ductílibus, et voce tubæ córneæ.
content.english: 97:5 Sing praise to the Lord on the harp, on the harp, and with the voice of a psalm: * with long trumpets, and sound of cornet.

content.latin: 97:6 Iubiláte in conspéctu regis Dómini: * moveátur mare, et plenitúdo eius: orbis terrárum, et qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 97:6 Make a joyful noise before the Lord our king: * let the sea be moved and the fulness thereof: the world and they that dwell therein.

content.latin: 97:8 Flúmina plaudent manu, simul montes exsultábunt a conspéctu Dómini: * quóniam venit iudicáre terram.

content.latin: 97:9 Iudicábit orbem terrárum in iustítia, * et pópulos in æquitáte.
content.english: 97:9 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with equity.

content.latin: 89:1 Dómine, refúgium factus es nobis: * ‡ a generatióne in generatiónem.
content.english: 89:1 Lord, thou hast been our refuge * ‡ from generation to generation.

content.latin: 89:2 Priúsquam montes fíerent, aut formarétur terra et orbis: * a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum tu es, Deus.
content.english: 89:2 Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world was formed; * from eternity and to eternity thou art God.

content.latin: 89:3 Ne avértas hóminem in humilitátem: * et dixísti: Convertímini, fílii hóminum.
content.english: 89:3 Turn not man away to be brought low: * and thou hast said: Be converted, O ye sons of men.

content.latin: 89:4 Quóniam mille anni ante óculos tuos, * tamquam dies hestérna, quæ prætériit,
content.english: 89:4 For a thousand years in thy sight * are as yesterday, which is past.

content.latin: 89:5 Et custódia in nocte, * quæ pro níhilo habéntur, eórum anni erunt.
content.english: 89:5 And as a watch in the night, * things that are counted nothing, shall their years be.

content.latin: 89:6 Mane sicut herba tránseat, mane flóreat, et tránseat: * véspere décidat, indúret et aréscat.
content.english: 89:6 In the morning man shall grow up like grass; in the morning he shall flourish and pass away: * in the evening he shall fall, grow dry, and wither.

content.latin: 89:7 Quia defécimus in ira tua, * et in furóre tuo turbáti sumus.
content.english: 89:7 For in thy wrath we have fainted away: * and are troubled in thy indignation.

content.latin: 89:8 Posuísti iniquitátes nostras in conspéctu tuo: * sǽculum nostrum in illuminatióne vultus tui.
content.english: 89:8 Thou hast set our iniquities before thy eyes: * our life in the light of thy countenance.

content.latin: 89:9 Quóniam omnes dies nostri defecérunt: * et in ira tua defécimus.
content.english: 89:9 For all our days are spent; * and in thy wrath we have fainted away.

content.latin: 89:9 Anni nostri sicut aránea meditabúntur: * dies annórum nostrórum in ipsis, septuagínta anni.
content.english: 89:9 Our years shall be considered as a spider: * the days of our years in them are threescore and ten years.

content.latin: 89:10 Si autem in potentátibus, octogínta anni: * et ámplius eórum, labor et dolor.
content.english: 89:10 But if in the strong they be fourscore years: * and what is more of them is labour and sorrow.

content.latin: 89:10 Quóniam supervénit mansuetúdo: * et corripiémur.
content.english: 89:10 For mildness is come upon us: * and we shall be corrected.

content.latin: 89:11 Quis novit potestátem iræ tuæ: * et præ timóre tuo iram tuam dinumeráre?
content.english: 89:11 Who knoweth the power of thy anger, * and for thy fear can number thy wrath?

content.latin: 89:12 Déxteram tuam sic notam fac: * et erudítos corde in sapiéntia.
content.english: 89:12 So make thy right hand known: * and men learned in heart, in wisdom.

content.latin: 89:13 Convértere, Dómine, úsquequo? * et deprecábilis esto super servos tuos.
content.english: 89:13 Return, O Lord, how long? * and be entreated in favour of thy servants.

content.latin: 89:14 Repléti sumus mane misericórdia tua: * et exsultávimus, et delectáti sumus ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 89:14 We are filled in the morning with thy mercy: * and we have rejoiced, and are delighted all our days.

content.latin: 89:15 Lætáti sumus pro diébus, quibus nos humiliásti: * annis, quibus vídimus mala.
content.english: 89:15 We have rejoiced for the days in which thou hast humbled us: * for the years in which we have seen evils.

content.latin: 89:16 Réspice in servos tuos, et in ópera tua: * et dírige fílios eórum.
content.english: 89:16 Look upon thy servants and upon their works: * and direct their children.

content.latin: 89:17 Et sit splendor Dómini, Dei nostri, super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos: * et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: 89:17 And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us: and direct thou the works of our hands over us; * yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

content.latin: 35:2 Dixit iniústus ut delínquat in semetípso: * non est timor Dei ante óculos eius.

content.english: 35:5 He hath devised iniquity on his bed, * he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.

content.latin: 35:6 Dómine, in cælo misericórdia tua: * et véritas tua usque ad nubes.
content.english: 35:6 O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, * and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.

content.latin: 35:7 Iustítia tua sicut montes Dei: * iudícia tua abýssus multa.
content.english: 35:7 Thy justice is as the mountains of God, * thy judgments are a great deep.

content.latin: 35:7 Hómines, et iuménta salvábis, Dómine: * quemádmodum multiplicásti misericórdiam tuam, Deus.
content.english: 35:7 Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord: * O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God!

content.latin: 35:8 Fílii autem hóminum, * in tégmine alárum tuárum sperábunt.
content.english: 35:8 But the children of men * shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.

content.latin: 35:9 Inebriabúntur ab ubertáte domus tuæ: * et torrénte voluptátis tuæ potábis eos.
content.english: 35:9 They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; * and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.

content.latin: 35:10 Quóniam apud te est fons vitæ: * et in lúmine tuo vidébimus lumen.
content.english: 35:10 For with thee is the fountain of life; * and in thy light we shall see light.

content.latin: 35:11 Præténde misericórdiam tuam sciéntibus te, * et iustítiam tuam his, qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 35:11 Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, * and thy justice to them that are right in heart.

content.latin: 35:12 Non véniat mihi pes supérbiæ: * et manus peccatóris non móveat me.
content.english: 35:12 Let not the foot of pride come to me, * and let not the hand of the sinner move me.

content.latin: 35:13 Ibi cecidérunt qui operántur iniquitátem: * expúlsi sunt, nec potuérunt stare.
content.english: 35:13 There the workers of iniquity are fallen, * they are cast out, and could not stand.

content.latin: 146:11 Beneplácitum est Dómino super timéntes eum: * et in eis, qui sperant super misericórdia eius.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
content.english: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

content.latin: 22:2 Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
content.english: 22:2 He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

content.latin: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
content.english: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

content.latin: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
content.english: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

content.latin: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
content.english: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

content.latin: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

content.latin: In monastério Vallis Castri, in Picéno, natális sancti Romuáldi Ravennátis, Anachorétæ et Monachórum Camaldulénsium Patris; qui collápsam in Itália eremíticam discíplinam restítuit ac mirífice propagávit. Eius tamen festívitas recólitur séptimo Idus Februárii, quo die sacræ ipsíus relíquiæ Fabriánum sunt translátæ.
content.english: At Milan, [in the first century,] the holy martyrs Gervase and Protase, brothers. The former, by order of the judge Astasius, was scourged with leaded whips for so long that he expired. The latter, after being scourged with rods, was beheaded. Through divine revelation their bodies were found by St. Ambrose. They were partly covered with blood, and as free from corruption as if they had been put to death that very day. When the translation took place, a blind man recovered his sight by touching their relics, and many persons possessed by demons were delivered.

content.latin: Arétii, in Túscia, sanctórum Mártyrum Gaudéntii Epíscopi, et Culmátii Diáconi, qui, témpore Valentiniáni, furóre Gentílium cæsi sunt.
content.english: At the monastery in the valley of Castro in Piceno, the birthday of St. Romuald, anchoret, a native of Ravenna. He was the founder of the Camaldolese monks, and he restored and greatly extended monastic discipline, which was much relaxed in Italy. His feast is observed on the 7th of February, on which day his sacred relics were transferred to Fabriano.

content.latin: Eódem die sancti Bonifátii, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui fuit beáti Romuáldi discípulus. content.english: At Arezzo in Tuscany, the holy martyrs Gaudentius, bishop, and Culmatius, deacon, who were murdered by the furious heathen, during the reign of Valentinian.

content.latin: Ravénnæ sancti Ursicíni Mártyris, qui, sub Paulíno Iúdice, post plúrima torménta, in Dómini confessióne pérmanens immóbilis, cápitis abscissióne martýrium complévit.
content.english: Also, St. Boniface, martyr, a disciple of blessed Romuald, who was sent by the Roman Pontiff, Gregory V, to preach the Gospel in Russia. Having passed through fire uninjured, and baptized the king and his people, he was killed by the enraged brother of the king, and thus gained the palm of martyrdom which he ardently desired.

content.english: 72:1 How good is God to Israel, to them that are of a right heart!

content.latin: 72:2 ‡ Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
content.english: 72:2 ‡ But my feet were almost moved; * my steps had wellnigh slipped.

content.latin: 72:3 Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.
content.english: 72:3 Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, * seeing the prosperity of sinners.

content.latin: 72:4 Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
content.english: 72:4 For there is no regard to their death, * nor is there strength in their stripes.

content.latin: 72:5 In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
content.english: 72:5 They are not in the labour of men: * neither shall they be scourged like other men.

content.latin: 72:6 Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
content.english: 72:6 Therefore pride hath held them fast: * they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.

content.latin: 72:7 Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
content.english: 72:7 Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: * they have passed into the affection of the heart.

content.latin: 72:8 Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
content.english: 72:8 They have thought and spoken wickedness: * they have spoken iniquity on high.

content.latin: 72:9 Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
content.english: 72:9 They have set their mouth against heaven: * and their tongue hath passed through the earth.

content.latin: 72:10 Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.
content.english: 72:10 Therefore will my people return here * and full days shall be found in them.

content.latin: 72:15 Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.

content.english: 72:24 Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, * and with thy glory thou hast received me.

content.latin: 72:25 Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?
content.english: 72:25 For what have I in heaven? * and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?

content.latin: 72:26 Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
content.english: 72:26 For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: * thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.

content.latin: 72:27 Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.
content.english: 72:27 For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: * thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.

content.latin: 72:28 Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
content.english: 72:28 But it is good for me to adhere to my God, * to put my hope in the Lord God:

content.latin: Psalmus 73(1-9) [1]
73:1 Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
content.english: 73:1 O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: * why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?

content.latin: 73:2 Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.
content.english: 73:2 Remember thy congregation, * which thou hast possessed from the beginning.

content.latin: 73:2 Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
content.english: 73:2 The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: * mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.

content.latin: 73:3 Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
content.english: 73:3 Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.

content.latin: 73:4 Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
content.english: 73:4 And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.

content.latin: 73:5 Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
content.english: 73:5 They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.

content.latin: 73:6 Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.
content.english: 73:6 As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.

content.latin: 73:7 Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
content.english: 73:7 They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.

content.latin: 73:8 Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
content.english: 73:8 They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.

content.latin: 73:9 Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
content.english: 73:9 Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.

content.latin: 73:10 Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
content.english: 73:10 How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?

content.latin: 73:11 Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
content.english: 73:11 Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand * out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?

content.latin: 73:12 Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
content.english: 73:12 But God is our king before ages: * he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.

content.latin: 73:13 Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
content.english: 73:13 Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: * thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.

content.latin: 73:14 Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
content.english: 73:14 Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: * thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.

content.latin: 73:15 Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
content.english: 73:15 Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: * thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.

content.latin: 73:16 Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
content.english: 73:16 Thine is the day, and thine is the night: * thou hast made the morning light and the sun.

content.latin: 73:17 Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
content.english: 73:17 Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: * the summer and the spring were formed by thee.

content.latin: 73:18 Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:18 Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: * and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.

content.latin: 73:19 Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
content.english: 73:19 Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: * and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.

content.latin: 73:20 Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
content.english: 73:20 Have regard to thy covenant: * for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.

content.latin: 73:21 Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
content.english: 73:21 Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: * the poor and needy shall praise thy name.

content.latin: 73:22 Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
content.english: 73:22 Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: * remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.

content.latin: 73:23 Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
content.english: 73:23 Forget not the voices of thy enemies: * the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.

content.latin: 74:2 Confitébimur tibi, Deus: * confitébimur, et invocábimus nomen tuum.
content.english: 74:2 We will praise thee, O God: * we will praise, and we will call upon thy name.

content.latin: 74:3 Narrábimus mirabília tua: * cum accépero tempus, ego iustítias iudicábo.
content.english: 74:3 We will relate thy wondrous works: * when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.

content.latin: 74:4 Liquefácta est terra, et omnes qui hábitant in ea: * ego confirmávi colúmnas eius.
content.english: 74:4 The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: * I have established the pillars thereof.

content.latin: 74:5 Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere: * et delinquéntibus: Nolíte exaltáre cornu:
content.english: 74:5 I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: * and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.

content.latin: 74:6 Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum: * nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
content.english: 74:6 Lift not up your horn on high: * speak not iniquity against God.

content.latin: 74:7 Quia neque ab Oriénte, neque ab Occidénte, neque a desértis móntibus: * quóniam Deus iudex est.
content.english: 74:7 For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills: * for God is the judge.

content.latin: 74:8 Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat: * quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto.
content.english: 74:8 One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up: * for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture.

content.latin: 74:9 Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc: verúmtamen fæx eius non est exinaníta: * bibent omnes peccatóres terræ.
content.english: 74:9 And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: * all the sinners of the earth shall drink.

content.latin: 74:10 Ego autem annuntiábo in sǽculum: * cantábo Deo Iacob.
content.english: 74:10 But I will declare for ever: * I will sing to the God of Jacob.

content.latin: 74:11 Et ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam: * et exaltabúntur córnua iusti.
content.english: 74:11 And I will break all the horns of sinners: * but the horns of the just shall be exalted.

content.latin: 75:11 Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.

content.english: 135:1 Praise the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:2 Confitémini Deo deórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:2 Praise ye the God of gods: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:3 Confitémini Dómino dominórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:3 Praise ye the Lord of lords: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:4 Qui facit mirabília magna solus: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:4 Who alone doth great wonders: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:5 Qui fecit cælos in intelléctu: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:5 Who made the heavens in understanding: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:6 Qui firmávit terram super aquas: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:6 Who established the earth above the waters: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:7 Qui fecit luminária magna: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:7 Who made the great lights: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:8 Solem in potestátem diéi: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:8 The sun to rule the day: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:9 Lunam, et stellas in potestátem noctis: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:9 The moon and the stars to rule the night: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:10 Qui percússit Ægýptum cum primogénitis eórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:10 Who smote Egypt with their firstborn: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:11 Qui edúxit Israël de médio eórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:11 Who brought out Israel from among them: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:12 In manu poténti, et brácchio excélso: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:12 With a mighty hand and with a stretched out arm: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:13 Qui divísit Mare Rubrum in divisiónes: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:13 Who divided the Red sea into parts: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:14 Et edúxit Israël per médium eius: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:14 And brought out Israel through the midst thereof: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:15 Et excússit Pharaónem, et virtútem eius in Mari Rubro: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:15 And overthrew Pharao and his host in the Red sea: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:16 Qui tradúxit pópulum suum per desértum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:16 Who led his people through the desert: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:17 Qui percússit reges magnos: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:17 Who smote great kings: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:18 Et occídit reges fortes: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:18 And slew strong kings: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:19 Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:19 Sehon king of the Amorrhites: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:20 Et Og, regem Basan: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:20 And Og king of Basan: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:21 Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:21 And he gave their land for an inheritance: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:22 Hereditátem Israël, servo suo: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:22 For an inheritance to his servant Israel: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:23 Quia in humilitáte nostra memor fuit nostri: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:23 For he was mindful of us in our affliction: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:24 Et redémit nos ab inimícis nostris: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:24 And he redeemed us from our enemies: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:25 Qui dat escam omni carni: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 135:25 Who giveth food to all flesh: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 135:26 Confitémini Deo cæli: * quóniam in ætérnum misericórdia eius.

content.latin: 136:1 Super flúmina Babylónis, illic sédimus et flévimus: * cum recordarémur Sion:
content.english: 136:1 Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: * when we remembered Sion:

content.latin: 136:2 In salícibus in médio eius, * suspéndimus órgana nostra.
content.english: 136:2 On the willows in the midst thereof * we hung up our instruments.

content.latin: 136:3 Quia illic interrogavérunt nos, qui captívos duxérunt nos, * verba cantiónum:
content.english: 136:3 For there they that led us into captivity required of us * the words of songs.

content.latin: 136:3 Et qui abduxérunt nos: * Hymnum cantáte nobis de cánticis Sion.
content.english: 136:3 And they that carried us away, said: * Sing ye to us a hymn of the songs of Sion.

content.latin: 136:4 Quómodo cantábimus cánticum Dómini * in terra aliéna?
content.english: 136:4 How shall we sing the song of the Lord * in a strange land?

content.latin: 136:5 Si oblítus fúero tui, Ierúsalem, * oblivióni detur déxtera mea.
content.english: 136:5 If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, * let my right hand be forgotten.

content.latin: 136:6 Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, * si non memínero tui:
content.english: 136:6 Let my tongue cleave to my jaws, * if I do not remember thee:

content.latin: 136:6 Si non proposúero Ierúsalem, * in princípio lætítiæ meæ.
content.english: 136:6 If I make not Jerusalem * the beginning of my joy.

content.latin: 136:7 Memor esto, Dómine, filiórum Edom, * in die Ierúsalem:
content.english: 136:7 Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom, * in the day of Jerusalem:

content.latin: 136:7 Qui dicunt: Exinaníte, exinaníte * usque ad fundaméntum in ea.
content.english: 136:7 Who say: Rase it, rase it, * even to the foundation thereof.

content.latin: 136:8 Fília Babylónis mísera: * beátus, qui retríbuet tibi retributiónem tuam, quam retribuísti nobis.
content.english: 136:8 O daughter of Babylon, miserable: * blessed shall he be who shall repay thee thy payment which thou hast paid us.

content.latin: 136:9 Beátus, qui tenébit, * et allídet párvulos tuos ad petram.
content.english: 136:9 Blessed be he that shall take * and dash thy little ones against the rock.

content.latin: 137:1 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo: * quóniam audísti verba oris mei.
content.english: 137:1 I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: * for thou hast heard the words of my mouth.

content.latin: 137:2 In conspéctu Angelórum psallam tibi: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum, et confitébor nómini tuo.
content.english: 137:2 I will sing praise to thee in the sight of the Angels: * I will worship towards thy holy temple, and I will give glory to thy name.

content.latin: 137:3 Super misericórdia tua, et veritáte tua: * quóniam magnificásti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum.
content.english: 137:3 For thy mercy, and for thy truth: * for thou hast magnified thy holy name

content.latin: 137:4 In quacúmque die invocávero te, exáudi me: * multiplicábis in ánima mea virtútem.
content.english: 137:4 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, hear me: * thou shalt multiply strength in my soul.

content.latin: 137:5 Confiteántur tibi, Dómine, omnes reges terræ: * quia audiérunt ómnia verba oris tui:
content.english: 137:5 May all the kings of the earth give glory to thee: * for they have heard all the words of thy mouth.

content.latin: 137:6 Et cantent in viis Dómini: * quóniam magna est glória Dómini.
content.english: 137:6 And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: * for great is the glory of the Lord.

content.latin: 137:7 Quóniam excélsus Dóminus, et humília réspicit: * et alta a longe cognóscit.
content.english: 137:7 For the Lord is high, and looketh on the low: * and the high he knoweth afar off.

content.latin: 137:8 Si ambulávero in médio tribulatiónis, vivificábis me: * et super iram inimicórum meórum extendísti manum tuam, et salvum me fecit déxtera tua.
content.english: 137:8 If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation, thou wilt quicken me: * and thou hast stretched forth thy hand against the wrath of my enemies: and thy right hand hath saved me.

content.latin: 137:9 Dóminus retríbuet pro me: * Dómine, misericórdia tua in sǽculum: ópera mánuum tuárum ne despícias.
content.english: 137:9 The Lord will repay for me: * thy mercy, O Lord, endureth for ever: O despise not the works of thy hands.

content.latin: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
content.english: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

content.latin: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
content.english: This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph

content.latin: Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
content.english: Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness

content.latin: Hac die lætus méruit suprémos
content.english: On this feast day year by year receiveth

content.latin: Laudis honóres.
content.english: Merited honors.

content.latin: Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
content.english: Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,

content.latin: Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
content.english: Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.

content.latin: Donec humános animávit auræ
content.english: While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,

content.latin: Spíritus artus.
content.english: Quickened his being.

content.latin: Cuius ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
content.english: Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,

content.latin: Ægra quæ passim iacuére membra,
content.english: Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,

content.latin: Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
content.english: Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,

content.latin: Restituúntur.
content.english: At his petition.

content.latin: Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
content.english: Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,

content.latin: Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
content.english: Chanting his praises with devout affection,

content.latin: Ut piis eius précibus iuvémur
content.english: That in his merits we may have a portion,

content.latin: Omne per ævum.
content.english: Now and forever.

content.latin: Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
content.english: His be the glory, power and salvation,

content.latin: Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
